_comment: BindCraft target settings - APPROACH C: extracellular crown / loop binder.
Site: the composite inter-protomer groove on the extracellular face. The key
observation from 4MT0 is that Loop 2 of one protomer packs directly against
Loop 1 of its neighbour:
This two-protomer groove buries far more surface than either loop alone and is
much more rigid, which is the main defence against the flexible-loop false
positives you have been getting. Design against the groove, NOT a single loop.
Anchor residues chosen for exposure (Shrake-Rupley on the trimer):
F326 SASA 149 A^2   exposed Phe - the best single anchor on the surface
W333 SASA  78 A^2   exposed Trp at the inter-protomer seam
L322 SASA 114 A^2   K327 SASA 126 A^2
L114 SASA  97 A^2   V119 SASA 102 A^2  (neighbouring protomer)
Loop 2 (auth 319-331, mature 299-311) = SVELGGLFKSGTG, the 13-aa epitope that
is conserved in >98% of gonococcal isolates and is engaged by bactericidal
antibodies on live cells. Accessibility here is experimentally established.
NOTE the crown protrudes only ~7-10 A above the outer-leaflet aromatic girdle
(F326, z=+59.5). Binders must approach axially from +z. Any design that wraps
below z=+58 is clashing with lipid/LOS - see scripts/filter_designs.py.
VERIFY key names against your installed BindCraft settings_target/*.json.
